issues.legal_issue: A claimant’s sibling relationship to a deceased hereditary trustee may be upheld when an admission of that relationship is supported by other evidence.
material_facts: The claimant asserted that she was the deceased trustee’s sister, while the opposing claimants disputed the relationship.
One opposing claimant had admitted in an affidavit, after the dispute began, that the claimant was the deceased trustee’s sister.
Witness testimony supported the claimant’s relationship, and the High Court accepted that testimony while rejecting contrary testimony.
The Supreme Court considered that the remaining evidence established the relationship even without the additional documentary evidence introduced in the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court upheld the finding that the claimant was the deceased trustee’s sister.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the admission as important evidence and assessed it together with supporting testimony and the rejection of contrary testimony. It did not decide whether the additional evidence had properly been admitted under Order 41, Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure, because the relevant order was unavailable; it held that the remaining evidence was sufficient.

rule.if: kinship_finding_appeal and admission_of_siblinghood and supporting_relationship_evidence and contrary_relationship_evidence_rejected

predicates.kinship_finding_appeal: The proceeding includes an appeal disputing a lower court’s determination of whether a claimant was related to a deceased person as a sibling.
predicates.admission_of_siblinghood: A party to the dispute admitted that the claimant was the deceased person’s sibling.
predicates.supporting_relationship_evidence: Witnesses or other evidence supported the claimed sibling relationship.
predicates.contrary_relationship_evidence_rejected: The evidence opposing the claimed relationship was rejected after assessment.

issues.definition: When an appeal disputes a sibling-relationship finding and an admission is supported by other evidence while contrary evidence is rejected, the claimant’s relationship is proved.

issues.legal_issue: Succession to a hereditary trusteeship of a private charity follows ordinary Hindu inheritance when the instrument’s prescribed line of succession has run its course and no contrary special custom applies.
material_facts: The trust was a hereditary trusteeship connected with a private charity, and no special custom governing succession was pleaded or proved.
The original instrument appointed the founder’s foster son and wife, then provided for the foster son’s sons and, if they were absent, his descendants to succeed.
A later trustee took over and held the trusteeship until his death without issue; the instrument’s prescribed succession had already reached him.
The claimant was the deceased trustee’s sister, and the competing claimants were his nephews.
The claimant was a nearer heir under the applicable ordinary Mitakshara inheritance rules, as altered by the Hindu Law of Inheritance Amendment Act, 1929.
issues.conclusion: The instrument’s succession directions ended when the later trustee took office; he became a fresh stock of descent, and the claimant was entitled to succeed to the trusteeship under ordinary Hindu inheritance law.
issues.legal_principle: For a hereditary trusteeship of a private charity, succession ordinarily follows Hindu inheritance law unless a contrary provision or special custom applies. The Court relied on Sethuramaswamiar v. Meruswamiar, which referred to Ramanathan Chetty v. Murugappa Chetty, for the passage of management of a private charity to the natural heirs where the original grant makes no contrary provision. It also relied on Sm. Angurbala Mullick v. Debabrata Mullick for applying changes to general inheritance law to succession to a religious office with an element of office. The Court held that the change to general inheritance law made by the Hindu Law of Inheritance Amendment Act, 1929, was to be recognized in succession to trusteeship, but expressly left undecided whether trusteeship is “property” within that Act.

rule.if: private_hereditary_charity_trustee_succession and no_special_succession_custom and instrument_named_limited_successors and later_trustee_assumed_office and claimant_is_sibling_and_nearer_heir

predicates.private_hereditary_charity_trustee_succe: The proceeding concerns succession to a hereditary trusteeship connected with a private charity.
predicates.no_special_succession_custom: No special custom governing succession to the trusteeship was pleaded or proved.
predicates.instrument_named_limited_successors: The instrument prescribed successors only through a specified line and did not prescribe a further line after the person who later held the trusteeship.
predicates.later_trustee_assumed_office: A person outside the instrument’s expressly named succession stages took over and held the trusteeship.
predicates.claimant_is_sibling_and_nearer_heir: The claimant was the deceased trustee’s sibling and was a nearer heir under the applicable ordinary inheritance rules than the competing claimants.

issues.definition: If a private hereditary charity trusteeship is disputed, no special succession custom applies, the instrument’s specified line ends after a later trustee takes office, and the claimant is that trustee’s sibling and nearer heir, the claimant succeeds to the trusteeship.
